title: Synthetic Theory Note: Procedural Control and Authorization
citation: Demonstration source created for this prototype; not a published theory article.

passages.text: When a formal procedure gives a central actor veto authority, operating units are expected to seek authorization before committing resources that cross unit boundaries.
Additional approval can reduce variance and unauthorized action, but under time pressure it ordinarily adds a queue and lengthens response unless the approval is only ceremonial.
The expectation weakens when local actions are reversible, the central actor rarely rejects requests, or coordination work occurs before the formal commitment.
